unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Standing mean-zero convention for the causal process in Section2.2. In T4.1 the approximation applies to noise Zi rather than observations Xi.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Similarly for a sequence of random variables $(X_n)_{n\ge1}$ and a positive sequence $y_n$, if $X_n/y_n\to0$ in probability, we write $X_n=o_{\mathbb P}(y_n)$, and if $X_n/y_n$ is stochastically bounded, we write $X_n=O_{\mathbb P}(y_n)$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: All theorem approximation errors use convergence in probability, not almost-sure convergence from the introductory classical KMT discussion.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
Let
\[
W^\diamond(t)=\sum_{i=1}^nw_i(t)\big(\mathbb B(\mathbb E(S_i^2))-\mathbb B(\mathbb E(S_{i-1}^2))\big)
\]
(4.1)
be the Gaussian process that we want to use to approximate $W(t)$, where $S_i=\sum_{j=1}^ie_j$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: The preceding W(t)=sum e_i w_i(t) concerns mean-zero errors e_i. This explicitly resolves S_i as the noise sum when T4.1 sets e_i=Z_i.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
Usually the block length $m$ is taken so as $m\to\infty$ with $m/n\to0$. Define for $1\le a,k,j\le\lceil n/m\rceil$,
\[
B_a:=\sum_{i=(a-1)m+1}^{am\wedge n}X_i;\quad T_k=\sum_{a=1}^kB_a^2+2\sum_{a=1}^{k-1}B_aB_{a+1};\quad R_j:=\mathbb I_{\{j/m\notin\mathbb N\}}\sum_{i=\lfloor j/m\rfloor m+1}^jX_i.
\]
(3.1)
Note that $S_j=\sum_{a=1}^kB_a+R_j$, where $k=\lfloor j/m\rfloor$. We shall estimate $\mathbb E(S_j^2)$ by the following ‘Block-based Running Variance’ (BRV) estimator $\mathcal T_j$ where
\[
\mathcal T_j:=T_{\lfloor j/m\rfloor}+R_j^2+2B_{\lfloor j/m\rfloor}R_j\quad\text{for all }1\le j\le n
\]
(3.2)
simultaneously.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Original BRV construction is contextual to T3.1–T3.2, not a premise of either theorem. Preserve its printed initial j range, though the later formula uses every j≤n, and flag the unprovided B0 convention.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Since $\mathcal T_j$’s may be negative, so instead of Brownian motion we use two-sided Brownian motion. A two-sided Brownian motion is defined as $\mathbb W(t)=\mathbb B_1(t)\mathbb1_{t\ge0}+\mathbb B_2(-t)\mathbb1_{t<0}$, where $\mathbb B_1$ and $\mathbb B_2$ are two independent standard Brownian motions starting at $0$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Empirical BRV evaluation can require negative times. Theorem3.2 itself uses ordinary Brownian motion at nonnegative true second moments.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: where $\mathbb P^*$ refers to the conditional distribution after observing $X_1,\ldots,X_n$, and $\mathbb B_1(\cdot)$ is the same Brownian motion defining the positive half-line of $\mathbb W(\cdot)$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: This defines the bootstrap order symbol following (3.10); T3.2 instead states an unconditional little-o_P result.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: We emphasize that to avoid notational cumbersomeness, in (3.4) we have used same notation $C_p$ to denote multiple constants, each depending solely on $p$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Different occurrences of Cp in T3.1 need not be the same numeric constant.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: The classical uniform integrability condition for $(|X_t|^p)_t$ is $\sup_i\mathbb E(|X_i|^p\mathbb I_{\{|X_i|^p\ge k\}})\to0$ as $k\to\infty$. Note that Condition 2.2 is weaker.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Preserve the author’s comparison. With a fixed sequence and an unrestricted supremum over i, the printed conditions are equivalent by reparameterizing the truncation level. No triangular-array index restriction is silently inserted.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: In fact, our proof works for $A>1/2-1/q$ and matches their non-uniform bound for the corresponding case. A similar argument can be followed to yield a bound for a process satisfying $\mu_{p,A}<\infty$ for some general $A$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Remark3.2 describes a proof extension and uses an undefined q in this main-text sentence. T3.1 retains Condition2.1 with A>1; no unstated weaker theorem is substituted.
Source comparison has its inequality reversed for the printed zeta1=min{1,2−4/p}/(1+2A) and zeta2=min{1,2−4/p}/3. Keep the actual zeta1 formula in T3.2; do not change it to fit the prose.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: By the argument in Theorem 3.1 in [34], $\mathbb E[\widehat\mu_{h_n}(t)]-\mu(t)=h_n^2\mu''(t)\beta+O(h_n^3+n^{-1}h_n^{-1})$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Proof-local bias expansion helps check scale placement; it is not an extra theorem or a replacement for the full statement.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
Using (4.10) to construct simultaneous confidence band requires estimation of $\mu''(t)$. Following [48], we use the jackknife-based bias corrected estimator
\[
\widetilde\mu_{h_n}(t)=2\widehat\mu_{h_n}(t)-\widehat\mu_{h_n\sqrt2}(t).
\]
(4.11)
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Subsequent bias correction is separate from the uncorrected local linear estimator in T4.1. Bootstrap bands and wavelet/CUSUM applications in prose are not additional Theorem environments.

source_issues.note: The Gaussian processes coexist with an equal-joint-law copy on a possibly enriched probability space. The original variable notation suppresses this convention. The theorem rates are o_P, not the introductory classical almost-sure KMT rate.

Clipping at n^(1/p) defines X^oplus; S^oplus additionally subtracts the clipped means. T2.2’s second branch matches Cov(X^oplus) yet compares to original S. T2.4’s faster Brownian time is the second moment of the centered clipped sum, while its slower branch uses the original sum.

Condition2.3 diverges over blocks with m_n+1 terms; Condition2.4 bounds length-l second moments below by c l. A0 and A0-prime are different formulas. T2.4 and T3.2 require neither nonsingularity condition; T3.1 only uses A>1. No implication is turned into an additional dependency.

The paper calls Condition2.2 weaker than classical uniform integrability. As printed for a fixed sequence with sup over all i, taking a=1 and reparameterizing the truncation threshold yields the same criterion. Any triangular-array interpretation would need explicit index conventions absent here.

For a dependent process the curve j↦E(S_j²) can decrease. Evaluating Brownian motion at these times is meaningful, but successive differences indexed by observations need not be independent increments. Preserve the actual time-change formulas without inferring monotonicity from the section title.

T3.1 prints D_n≤n; its sums and division implicitly require a positive integer bandwidth. Different Cp occurrences may be different constants depending only on p. At p=4 use the first polynomial branch; the second branch and mu_(4,A) require p>4.

R_j in (3.1) is a leftover linear block sum, whereas R_k in (3.3) is a centered quadratic-block partial sum. The BRV formulas initially restrict j≤ceil(n/m) then use all j≤n, and use B0 when j<m without an explicit convention. These contextual formulas are not assumed in T3.1–T3.2.

Equation(3.10) is O_(P*) conditional on observations and uses estimated possibly negative BRV times. T3.2 is an unconditional o_P existence result at true second moments. Import only the numerical zeta1 definition, not the BRV estimator or a bootstrap-conditioning assumption.

With A>1 and p>2, the printed zeta1 denominator 1+2A exceeds3, hence zeta1<zeta2. The subsequent prose prints zeta2<zeta1. The census keeps the theorem’s actual exponent and flags this reversed comparison.

The source first states t_n<t_(n+1)=1 but then sets t_i=F^-1(i/n), giving t_n=1 for its positive density. Preserve both statements; do not silently replace i/n by i/(n+1). The theorem supremum itself is on the interior interval.

The source calls K a smooth symmetric kernel with bounded support and an integrated modulus condition. It does not separately state integral K=1 or nondegeneracy of S2 S0−S1². The displayed bias beta=one-half integral u²K(u)du uses the usual normalized-kernel interpretation; do not insert unquoted assumptions into the original statement.

In the trend model Xi=mu(t_i)+Zi, the approximation assumptions apply to Zi and Si in the Gaussian increments is its noise partial sum, as resolved by (4.1). S_j(t) instead denotes deterministic kernel-weighted design moments. Q_n in T3.1 and Q_h(t) in T4.1 are unrelated reused symbols.

statement_local_bindings.T2.1: Independent mean-zero variables, bounded p norms, p>2 and some gamma≥2 with the complete minimum-moment condition (2.1). Uses ordinary S_i and Brownian time E(S_i²). No causal representation, dependence norm, Condition2.2 or block variance assumption is imported. Coupling-space convention applies.
statement_local_bindings.T2.2: Mean-zero causal process, Conditions2.1–2.3 and A>A0. First Gaussian covariance matches original Xi with n^(1/p)sqrt(log n) rate. Second covariance matches clipped Xi^oplus while the approximation still targets original Si at n^(1/p). Gaussian means are not separately specified in the printed theorem; no independent-increment conclusion is added.
statement_local_bindings.T2.3: Conditions2.1,2.2,2.4 and the distinct A0-prime cutoff; original covariance matching and n^(1/p) rate. Does not explicitly assume Condition2.3 or use clipping.
statement_local_bindings.T2.4: Conditions2.1,2.2 and A>A0 only; no nonsingularity. One Brownian approximation uses E[(S_j^oplus)²] with centered clipping and the faster rate; the original E(S_j²) time has an additional sqrt(log n).
statement_local_bindings.T2.5: Inherit T2.3 assumptions: decay with A>A0-prime, truncated UI, and linear block variance lower bound. The conclusion is Brownian evaluation at original partial-sum second moments; do not import the Gaussian-process covariance-matching conclusion as a premise.
statement_local_bindings.T3.1: Mean-zero causal process under Condition2.1, p>2 and A>1. Banded bounded coefficients define Q_n,V_k and centered R_k. For 2<p≤4 retain the x^(-p/2)n D_n^(p/4) mu_(p,A)^p term; for p>4 retain D_n^(p/2−1) and the exponential term with mu_(4,A)^4. No UI, nondegeneracy, Gaussian coupling or estimated-variance assumption.
statement_local_bindings.T3.2: Mean-zero causal process, Condition2.1 with A>1, and Condition2.2. Zeta1=min{1,2−4/p}/(1+2A) is taken from preceding text. Brownian coupling has an unconditional little-o_P rate n^((1−A zeta1)/2)sqrt(log n). No empirical BRV input or conditional law is required.
statement_local_bindings.T4.1: Trend model on the quantile design, C³ mu and f with density bounds C1,C2, and preceding kernel assumption (4.9). T2.4 assumptions apply to centered noise Zi. Si=sum_{j≤i}Zj in Yi=B(E(Si²))−B(E(S_(i−1)²)), S0=0; use the same local-linear weights to form Q_h. S_j(t) denotes distinct design moments. Interior supremum, bias constant, h→0, h^4=O(n^(1/p−1)), nh→infinity and the full error scale remain intact.

ambient_prerequisites: Real-valued random variables, joint distributions, iid innovations, measurable causal maps, expectation, covariance, Brownian motion, Gaussian processes, enriched-space coupling, Lp norms and convergence in probability.

For dependent-process theorems the Section2.2 mean-zero convention applies. T2.1 independently states its own mean-zero/independence/moment conditions; it is a locally labeled theorem even though attributed to earlier work.
Covariance-matching processes and Brownian evaluations are distinct constructions. True second moments are nonnegative but not necessarily monotone in the observation index.

Kernel functions, C³ smoothness, deterministic quantile grids, matrix-free local-linear weights, interior intervals and bandwidth sequences. Standard Brownian B(0)=0 and empty partial sum S0=0 resolve T4.1’s first increment.
extraction_policy: All eight complete main-text Theorems. Preserve every original/truncated and moment-range branch, original definitions, and source limitations. Appendix bodies and proof certification excluded.
